title: Which floor is the lift attendant on in each case?
description: Two sets of tokens are cleaned up by taking away the zero pairs. The tokens left give the floor of the lift attendant, and the same tokens give the addition statement.
teaching_notes: One idea: cancel the zero pairs, and the tokens left give both the floor and the addition. Watch for students who write the number of tokens left without the sign that matches their colour.

video_script.why: The child cancels zero pairs in two sets of tokens and reads the floor and the addition statement from the tokens left.
video_script.substitution: Match each negative token with a positive token, take away the zero pairs, and read the floor from the tokens left.
video_script.anchor: the lift attendant's pocket of positive and negative tokens
video_script.payoff_line: The floors are negative two and positive three.

final_answer.spoken: floor negative two with three plus negative five, and floor positive three with six plus negative three

maths_rules: first set: 3 positive and 5 negative tokens: (+3) + (−5)
3 zero pairs are taken away; 5 − 3 = 2 negative tokens stay, so Floor −2 and (+3) + (−5) = −2
second set: 6 positive and 3 negative tokens: (+6) + (−3)
3 zero pairs are taken away; 6 − 3 = 3 positive tokens stay, so Floor +3 and (+6) + (−3) = +3
check: 2 negative tokens + 3 zero pairs = 5 negative and 3 positive tokens; 3 positive tokens + 3 zero pairs = 6 positive and 3 negative tokens
video_script.design: Two sets of tokens on one board. Zero pairs are ringed and taken away, and a lift needle shows the floor the tokens left point to. The check puts the zero pairs back.

<bookmark mark='second'/>In the second case, it holds six positive tokens and three negative tokens.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>On what floor is the lift attendant in each case?

narration: <bookmark mark='pair'/>A positive token and a negative token together are worth zero.
<bookmark mark='name'/>Such a pair is called a zero pair. Taking it away does not change the floor.

narration: <bookmark mark='tokens'/>Step one, take the first set, three positive and five negative tokens.
<bookmark mark='pairs'/>Match each positive token with a negative token. That gives three zero pairs, and we take them away.
<bookmark mark='left'/>Five take away three leaves two negative tokens.

marks.pairs: each red token joins a green token and the 3 zero pairs fade out

beats.colours: positive tokens = green, negative tokens = red
narration: <bookmark mark='tokens'/>Step two, take the second set, six positive and three negative tokens.
<bookmark mark='pairs'/>Match each negative token with a positive token. That gives three zero pairs, and we take them away.
<bookmark mark='left'/>Six take away three leaves three positive tokens.

beats.on_screen: Step 3: the colour left tells the side of ground: red left means below ground, green left means above ground; the floor is the number of tokens left with that sign

beats.colours: positive tokens = green, negative tokens = red
narration: <bookmark mark='needle'/>Step three, read the floor from the colour left. Red tokens left mean below the ground floor. Green tokens left mean above it.
<bookmark mark='state'/>The addition is the two counts we began with, written with their signs.

beats.on_screen: Step 4, check: tokens left + zero pairs put back = the tokens we began with; 2 red + 3 pairs gives 3 green and 5 red; 3 green + 3 pairs gives 6 green and 3 red

<bookmark mark='same'/>Two negative tokens and three zero pairs make five negative and three positive tokens again.
<bookmark mark='again'/>Three positive tokens and three zero pairs make six positive and three negative tokens again.

marks.ans: the two floors Floor −2 and Floor +3 are written and boxed
marks.one: the first addition (+3) + (−5) = −2 is written beside the first set
marks.two: the second addition (+6) + (−3) = +3 is written beside the second set

narration: <bookmark mark='ans'/>The floors are negative two and positive three.
<bookmark mark='one'/>Positive three plus negative five is negative two.
<bookmark mark='two'/>Positive six plus negative three is positive three.
